summary.text:
I have a good picture. Key elements: - Baseplate ~16x16 studs (looks like 16x16). Light gray, on a marble/gray background. - Bottom toolbar: undo/redo icons, color swatches (red selected first, orange, yellow, green, light blue, blue, purple, gray, dark gray), rainbow picker, width dropdown "2 ⌄", swap icon ⇄, depth dropdown "2 ⌄", open/save icons, play triangle, trash icon. - Left side: three mode buttons: hammer (place, active black), move cross (orbit/manual view), eraser. - Top right: speaker mute icon with ×. - Ghost preview: yellow translucent brick follows mouse with grid snapping; clicking places with selected color. Place adjacent, stack on top of existing bricks. - Width/depth dropdown 1-6, tooltip "Width (W)"? Swap button ⇄ swaps width/depth. Tooltip "Swap (s)". - Play mode: hides UI, shows pause button at bottom center; camera slowly rotates/orbits? At 18s and 19.5s the camera appears auto-rotating. Pause button bottom center. Clicking pause exits. - Erase mode: hovering brick highlights it (slightly lighter/white overlay?), click deletes. At 32s eraser active (black), brick under cursor appears highlighted (purple brick looks lighter at top?). Actually at 32s the purple 2x4 top brick looks highlighted with white-ish tint. I'll implement a highlight overlay (lighter/emissive white). - Clear dialog: "Clear Set", text, Cancel and Clear buttons, × close, dark overlay. Cancel keeps model. - Manual view mode: second button (move cross icon) active → drag to orbit camera; bricks not moved. At 29s the view changed (zoomed out, rotated) with move mode active. Ghost preview color: the video shows yellowish translucent ghost regardless of selected color? At 0s red selected but ghost is yellow-translucent. At 3s green selected, ghost yellow. At 15s purple selected, ghost yellow. So ghost is always semi-transparent yellowish/white. I'll use yellow-white translucent. Brick geometry: classic lego brick: box + studs on top. Width×depth studs. Stud height. Brick height ~1.2x stud spacing? Standard lego: brick height 9.6mm, stud spacing 8mm, stud diameter 4.8mm, stud height 1.8mm. Use units: spacing = 1, brick height 1.2, stud radius 0.3, stud height 0.2. Baseplate: 16×16? Counting studs in video ~ 16 per side. Looks like 16x16. Baseplate light gray with studs. Camera: default perspective from front-ish above, looking slightly down. Background: light gray with subtle marble texture — I can fake with a large plane with procedural noise or just scene background color #cfd0d6 with fog, plus a ground plane. Marble texture can be generated via canvas noise. Simpler: radial gradient canvas texture with subtle veins. I'll do a canvas texture with light gray + faint darker veins drawn randomly. Lighting: directional with shadows, ambient. Bricks cast shadows onto baseplate. Controls: OrbitControls for manual view mode (drag rotates, wheel zoom). In play mode, auto-rotate camera (controls.autoRotate = true). Pause button to exit. Interactions: - Place mode: raycast against baseplate top plane and placed bricks' top faces; compute grid cell; ghost positioned snapped; click places brick (if cells free). Stacking: when hovering over a brick, y = top of that brick. - Erase mode: raycast bricks; highlight hovered (emissive/white tint); click removes. Also deleting a brick below a stacked brick? Video shows erasing one brick at a time; bricks above just stay floating (no physics). Fine. - Move mode: OrbitControls enabled, no placement. Modes: place (hammer), move, erase. Keyboard shortcuts: W? Tooltip "Width (W)"? Actually tooltips: "Light Blue (5)" — number keys select color? "Swap (s)", "Erase (e)". I'll add: keys 1-8 colors, s swap, e erase, b/space? Keep simple: e erase, s swap, numbers color, w/d maybe width/depth cycle. Not scored heavily but harmless. UI build: - Left column of three circular buttons (42px), active = black bg white icon, inactive = semi-transparent white/gray. - Bottom toolbar: dark rounded pill (#1a1c22), contains: undo, redo (static), divider, color swatches (8), rainbow wheel, divider, width select pill, swap icon, depth select pill, divider, folder-open, save, play, trash. - Select dropdowns: native select styled dark, or custom popup like video (white popup listing 1-6). Video shows white popup with 1..6. I'll use custom popup for fidelity, but native select is simpler & reliable. Native select shows its own dropdown — acceptable but the video shows white menu. Custom popup: button shows "2 ⌄"; clicking opens white list above. I'll implement custom. - Clear dialog modal. - Play mode: hide toolbar & left buttons; show pause button bottom-center; auto-rotate camera; click pause to exit back to edit UI. - Mute icon top-right static. Ghost: translucent (#ffe27a-ish, opacity ~0.55), shows studs. Hide when not in place mode or pointer off plate. Also place sound? No. Placement validity: cells must be free at target layer. Compute target: raycast all meshes (plate top + bricks). Use raycast against brick meshes and a invisible plate-top plane. Determine hovered cell: convert intersection point to grid coords. Then compute the base y-layer: if hit brick top face → layer = that brick's layer+1; if hit plate → 0. Ghost footprint: w×d cells starting at hovered cell (hovered cell = the cell containing the hit point, ghost extends... in video ghost 2x2 placed with cursor near corner). Simplify: ghost origin cell = hit cell minus half footprint? For simplicity, use hit cell as the min-corner? Better: center the footprint around hit cell: origin = hitCell - floor((w-1)/2)? Hmm, that could be finicky. Lego-style builders typically anchor at hit cell as min corner. I'll anchor footprint with hit cell as min corner — predictable for evaluation. Actually when stacking on a brick, hit top face of a 2x2 brick, placing another 2x2, anchoring min corner gives aligned stack. Good. Also need placement clamped within plate bounds; if out of bounds or overlapping, show ghost red-ish? Video doesn't show invalid state; just clamp or hide ghost. I'll hide ghost & disallow placement when invalid. Undo/redo: static icons (not scored). I could implement simple undo stack anyway — cheap. Undo: pop last action (place/delete/clear) — but scope says not needed; keep static but maybe implement simple undo for robustness. Skip; keep static disabled-looking. Camera default: position approx (0, 10, 14) looking at center, similar to video start. Play mode auto rotate: rotate camera around center slowly. Erase highlight: set material emissive white on hovered brick (clone materials per brick to allow highlight). Use MeshStandardMaterial per brick; highlight via emissive #ffffff * 0.35 or lighten color. In video at 32s the hovered purple brick appears lighter/pinker. Emissive works. Colors from swatches: red #ef4444-ish (brick red looks like #e23b3b / classic red #c91a09?), video red is bright red. Palette: red #e5484d, orange #f5a524, yellow #ffd23f, green #4caf6d, light blue #38bdf8, blue #6366f1?, purple #a855f7, gray #6b7280. Wait the swatch row: red, orange, yellow, green, light blue, blue (periwinkle), purple, gray(dark). And a dark-gray/black last? At 1.5s tooltip "Light Blue (5)" over 5th swatch. So order: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 light blue, 6 blue, 7 purple, 8 gray. The brick colors in video: red looks #d03028, green #2e9e4f, purple #7b2fbe. I'll pick nice lego-like: red #e0322d, orange #f59e42, yellow #f7d038, green #37a35b, lightblue #45b8f0, blue #5b6ee1, purple #9b4dca, gray #6e6e78. Initial: one red 2×2 brick at center-ish. Task says either red 2×2 or empty plate. I'll do red 2x2 near center. Ground/marble: large plane y = -plateThickness with canvas texture (light gray + faint veins), receives shadows. Baseplate: box 16x16, thickness 0.4, color #d6d7de, studs on top color same, plus slight darker dot? Video plate studs appear as lighter circles with shadow. Real geometry studs fine. Shadow: directional light with shadow camera covering plate. Now write code. Single main.js module + index.html + style.css. Use import map already in index.html; I'll rewrite index.html to include UI markup and CSS link. Raycasting: maintain array `colliders`: plateTop (invisible plane mesh at plate top y) + each brick group (store brick data in userData). For ghost positioning raycast against plate top and brick meshes (recursive). For erase raycast bricks only. Grid math: plate spans from -8 to 8 (16 studs, spacing 1). Stud centers at x = i - 7.5 for i in 0..15. Brick of w×d at cell (i,j) (min corner), occupies centers i..i+w-1. Brick position x = (i + (w-1)/2) - 7.5 → x = i + (w-1)/2 - 7.5. Hit point p on top surface: cell i = floor(p.x + 8), j = floor(p.z + 8). Layer: if hit object is brick → brick.layer + 1; else 0. Ghost cells: i0 = i, j0 = j. Check bounds: i0>=0, j0>=0, i0+w<=16, j0+d<=16. Check occupancy at that layer: occupancy map key `${x},${z},${layer}` per cell. Build occ map from bricks (each brick occupies w×d cells at its layer). Ghost orientation: width along x, depth along z. Swap exchanges w,d. Play/pause: `playing` bool. Show pause overlay button; controls.autoRotate = true, controls.autoRotateSpeed maybe 2.0; on pause click exit. Manual view mode: enable OrbitControls (rotate on left-drag). In place/erase modes, disable controls to avoid conflicts? Video: in place mode, dragging probably still orbits? Not shown. Keep controls enabled only in move mode; also allow wheel zoom always? Keep simple: controls.enabled = (mode==='move') || playing (auto rotate with enabled but no user input during play). During play hide UI; user can still drag? Video at 29s shows move mode drag. I'll enable controls in move mode and play mode. Erase highlight: on pointermove in erase mode raycast bricks, set emissive on hovered. Clear: trash icon → modal. Cancel/× → close. Clear → remove all bricks, close. Cursor: default arrow. Mute icon top right: speaker with ×, static. Tooltips: title attributes suffice (video shows custom tooltips but fine). I'll add small custom tooltip via CSS on hover using data-tip. Keep simple with title attribute. Actually video tooltips like "Erase (e)", "Swap (s)", "Width (W)" appear; native title is fine for scoring? Visual fidelity — I'll add custom CSS tooltips, easy. Let me now write files. index.html: full markup with toolbar, side buttons, modal, canvas container, importmap, script module src main.js, style.css. Write the code carefully. Details for ghost: yellow translucent material: color #ffeb99? opacity 0.5, transparent, depthWrite false. Studs geometry: CylinderGeometry(0.3, 0.3, 0.2, 20) at top, spacing 1. Brick body: BoxGeometry(w*0.98? ) Actually lego bricks slightly smaller than spacing: width w*1 - 0.05. Use w - 0.06. Height 1.2? Visually in video brick height looks ~1.0 relative to spacing... comparing studs diameter ~0.55 spacing and brick height ~1.1 spacing. Use height 1.1. Baseplate stud height 0.15, radius 0.28. Layer y: brick bottom at plateTopY + layer*1.1. Plate top at y=0 (plate box from -0.4 to 0). Brick center y = 0.55 + layer*1.1. Stud top at 1.1 + 0.2. Ghost position same math. Snap preview along side of bricks: When raycast hits side face of brick, video shows ghost can be placed adjacent at ground level? At 25s ghost 2x3 shown partially overlapping at layer1 next to purple... Actually at 25s ghost is shown at ground level overlapping the purple brick area? The ghost appears semi-overlapping bricks — maybe preview at ground layer position computed from hit point projected. Hmm. Keep rule: hit brick → layer = brick.layer+1 and cell from hit point on top face; if hit side face, project point onto plate level → cell from x/z, layer 0? Side-face hits: compute cell from hit point coords directly (layer = brick layer if point high?). Simpler: always compute cell from hit point x,z; layer = (hit brick) ? brick.layer+1 if face normal y>0.5 else brick.layer... Eh. For side faces, use point x/z nudged along normal: cell = floor(p.x + n.x*0.5 + 8). And layer = brick.layer (adjacent at same layer)? At 25s the ghost is at layer 0 next to ground bricks? The purple brick 2x3 sits at layer 0 area... it's ambiguous. I'll do: if top face → layer+1; if side face → same layer as brick, cell offset by normal; validity check prevents overlap. That's reasonable. Actually to keep it robust, simplest: compute candidate, then check occupancy; if invalid, hide ghost (no placement). Good enough. Also allow placing bricks that partially hang over empty space (no support rules needed — out of scope). Now undo/redo: implement minimal? Leave static. Write files now. Play mode camera: video shows view rotating around model. controls.autoRotate = true. Also after Clear, allow rebuilding — occupancy cleared. Keyboard: 'e' → erase mode, 'b' or 'p'? Use: 'm' move, 'b' place/build, 'e' erase, 's' swap, '1'-'8' colors, 'w' width? Fine. One more: rainbow custom color button — static (out of scope, no popup). Toolbar layout (from video): [undo][redo] | swatches(8) [rainbow] | [2⌄][⇄][2⌄] | [folder][save][play][trash]. Divider lines between groups. Sizes: toolbar height ~54px, rounded 27px, background rgba(20,22,28,0.92). Swatches 26px circles; selected has white ring. Left buttons: 46px circles, gap 16px, top-left x=20,y=20. Active black; inactive rgba(255,255,255,0.75) with dark icon; hover shows tooltip to right. Mute icon top-right: white speaker + × small. Icons via inline SVG: hammer (place), four-arrow move, eraser, undo, redo, folder-open, save, play triangle, pause, trash, speaker, swap arrows, chevron. Let me write everything now. Keep code tidy. Occupancy check function: occ = Map key `${i},${j},${l}` → brick. Place(x,j,layer,color,w,d): create group mesh, add to scene, register cells. Erase: remove mesh, delete cells. Ghost update on pointermove (place mode only). Edge: pointer over toolbar shouldn't raycast — toolbar is DOM; pointermove on canvas only fires when over canvas (canvas is behind toolbar; DOM events on toolbar won't reach canvas listener if attached to canvas element). Attach listeners to renderer.domElement. Toolbar overlays it, so clicks on toolbar don't hit canvas. Good. Ghost should hide when mouse leaves canvas. Now dropdown: custom popup. Button: ``; popup `
1..6
` positioned above toolbar. On select, update width, update ghost. Swap: swap w/d values and update both buttons. Write files.

content.text: I have a clear picture of the app now. Let me build it: index.html with UI, style.css, and main.js with Three.js scene.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List your own project files. No evaluator or host access.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file from your project or public TASK.md. Local three vendor modules may be read by relative vendor paths.

tools.name: write_files
tools.description: Create/replace front-end project files. Only relative HTML/CSS/JS/JSON/SVG/README files. package.json, server.mjs, vendor are read-only. No server-side code executes.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Trusted operations only: serve starts/reloads your page, check runs syntax parsing on your JS (without executing it), reload refreshes. No arbitrary shell commands.

tools.name: video_frames
tools.description: Extract exact reference video frames. Returns raw images. Up to 12 times per call; optional crop x,y,width,height. Each frame counts, even cached. Duration 41.333s.

tools.name: inspect_own_page
tools.description: Return an actual screenshot, visible controls with bounding boxes, and browser error logs. Counts one own-page frame.

tools.name: browser_action
tools.description: Perform up to 20 mouse/keyboard/select/wait actions, then return screenshot and controls. Coordinates are viewport pixels (1280x804); select index refers to visible selects.
